issue: C1's barge-in requirement (specs/behavioral-spec.md C1 'INTERRUPTION' bullet) says barge-in MUST 'send Telnyx {"event":"clear"} + STOP our outbound edge-tts/ffmpeg send loop + drop the local playback buffer.' The implementation only sends the clear event; it never stops the send LOOP. `respond()` (lines 41-56) streams the LLM response and, for EACH completed sentence, calls `await tts(sentence, lang)` then `await send(audio)` inside the `onToken` callback and the trailing `flush()` loop — with ZERO check of `botSpeaking` (or any cancellation token) between sentences. `pushCallerFrame` (lines 59-76) sets the shared `botSpeaking` flag to `false` and fires `sendClear()` on barge-in, but that flag is never re-read by the already-running `respond()` call, so `respond()` keeps synthesizing+sending every remaining sentence of the OLD (interrupted) answer after the Telnyx `clear` event has already fired. Worse: `server.js`'s carrier `on("message")` handler calls `convo.pushCallerFrame(pcm16)` WITHOUT awaiting it (server.js:435, fire-and-forget with only a `.catch`), so while one `respond()` is mid-flight the VAD can independently endpoint a NEW caller utterance and start a SECOND, concurrent `respond()` call (via a later `pushCallerFrame` invocation) — nothing cancels or joins the first. The two `respond()` invocations' TTS/`send()` calls can then interleave, producing audio from the interrupted answer bleeding into/after the new answer. `server.js`'s `genId` counter (server.js:387-397) only halts the FRAME LOOP of a single already-in-flight `send()` call if `genId` changes DURING that specific call's 20ms-per-frame loop; it does nothing to prevent `respond()`'s async generator from issuing brand-new `send()` calls (each of which gets its OWN fresh `genId` and therefore runs to completion) for subsequent sentences after the barge-in already happened.

evidence.lines: 41-56 (respond, no cancellation check), 59-76 (pushCallerFrame sets botSpeaking=false but respond() never reads it again)
evidence.corroborating: apps/life-call/server.js:435 (convo.pushCallerFrame(pcm16).catch(...) — NOT awaited, so pushCallerFrame invocations for successive incoming media frames run concurrently while a prior respond() is still in flight); apps/life-call/server.js:387-397 (genId guard only protects the CURRENT send() call's own frame loop, not future send() calls issued by the same still-running respond())
evidence.test_gap: apps/life-call/lib/compositional-voice.test.js:53-61 — the only barge-in test asserts `calls.sendClear >= 1` and nothing else; it never checks that no further tts()/send() calls occur after the clear, so it PASSES even though the bug above means audio keeps flowing after the clear. Hand-traced: in that exact test, `await p` (the interrupted c.start() promise) resolves AFTER sendClear() already fired, and its `await send(audio)` for the opening line still executes — i.e. audio is sent to the carrier after the clear in the test's own execution, but the test doesn't assert against it.

fix: Give createConversation a per-turn cancellation token (e.g. an incrementing `turnId`, closed over by respond()): capture `const myTurn = ++turnId` at the start of respond(), and before every tts()/send() call inside the onToken callback and the flush loop, bail out if `myTurn !== turnId` or `!botSpeaking`. On barge-in, bump `turnId` (in addition to setting botSpeaking=false) so ANY in-flight respond() from a stale turn stops issuing further sentences immediately. Also await pushCallerFrame in server.js's message handler (or explicitly serialize frame processing) so utterance detection cannot outrace an in-flight respond(). Add a test asserting that after barge-in mid-response, tts()/send() call counts do not increase for the remaining queued sentences of the interrupted turn.
